title: Error Handling Basics
description: Learn to handle network errors and GraphQL errors in Apollo Client for robust applications.

data.text: Apollo Client distinguishes between two types of errors: network errors and GraphQL errors. Network errors occur when the request cannot reach the server or the response is malformed. GraphQL errors occur when the server returns a 200 OK but includes errors in the response body, often due to validation or authorization failures.

items: NetworkError: Request failed to reach server or returned non-200 status.
GraphQLError: Server returned errors array in response.
ApolloError: Combined error wrapper containing both types.
data.title: Error Types
Handling errors

data.text: Always handle both error types. A GraphQL error might return partial data, while a network error means no data at all. Design your UI accordingly.
data.title: Error Strategy
Error Handling Key Points
points: Network errors prevent data retrieval entirely.
GraphQL errors may include partial data.
Use error policies to control error behavior.
data.takeaway: Robust error handling is essential for production Apollo Client applications.
